items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: And that's how Norman and I became friends, because he liked jazz

ctx.x: Well, all I knew, I used to take him around with us all the time and all I knew was he had gone to UCLA for a year or two, and he used to play pretty good tennis. And the big tennis court over on La Cienega just off of Wilshire, and this is where I really met him, you know, because this was where tennis players, you know, they're really gamblers, and that's where they used to have big gambling matches, and I took him over to meet this young black guy who was an excellent tennis player - but he had never had a…
And that's how Norman and I became friends, because he liked jazz, and he was always around -- but he started to give all the names of the musicians, and that is a fact.

Let me ask you something -- you said you were in trouble for jamming. Didn't the union have -- I know later, the union had a rule that if you pay a basic rhythm section or if you pay 3 musicians -- a leader and 2 others -- then you can get permission to have a jam session where everybody isn't paid. Was that in effect then?
